practice.foundation[4]: Off-booklet type. The booklet teaches the range but never asks students to reject an out-of-range coefficient; question 11 instead supplies a scatterplot and asks why perfect correlation is impossible.

practice.foundation[5]: Off-booklet type: no source question asks students to diagnose equating a gradient with r. Also, a generic line fitted by eye does not guarantee the exact sign identity used in the solution.

practice.foundation[7]: Off-booklet type: no source question asks why a curved relationship can have zero r. The solution also assumes symmetric sampling, which the stated interval alone does not establish.
practice.development[1]: Off-booklet type: no source question compares two supplied correlation coefficients to rank strength.

practice.development[3]: The prediction-usefulness part is supported by spreadsheet question 4(c), lines 2199–2204, but the additional request to explain what zero-like r does not imply is not a source question type. Restrict the assessed task to the supported prediction-usefulness part.

practice.development[4]: Off-booklet type: no source question checks consistency between a supplied gradient and r. The mathematical claim also requires a least-squares regression line with an intercept, rather than an unspecified line of best fit.
practice.development[6]: Off-booklet type: no source question ranks association strength by comparing two supplied coefficients.

practice.mastery[1]: Off-booklet combined type: the source separately asks for gradient interpretation and r interpretation, but never asks students to explain their interchangeability. Restrict this item to interpretation of the supplied r to retain the target skill.

practice.mastery[2]: Off-booklet type: no source question asks students to explain zero r for a curved relationship. The question says ten plots, but its figure contains eleven points; repair that inconsistency if retaining any adapted figure.

quiz.q4: Off-booklet recognition type: the source teaches the range but does not ask students to select an impossible value. Distractor explanations describe validity without naming the student's specific misconception.
quiz.q5: Off-booklet type: no source question asks students to diagnose substituting the gradient or intercept for r.

quiz.q7: Off-booklet type: no source question asks students to interpret zero r for a perfect curved relationship. The solution's cancellation argument additionally assumes symmetric sampling, although the given r itself is sufficient to choose the correct option.
quiz.q8: Off-booklet type: no source question compares two supplied coefficients to rank strength.
quiz.dq-11223: Off-booklet type: positive scaling invariance is neither taught nor asked in the supplied booklet. Remove or replace this item under the booklet-type rule.

theory: Specify magnitude as $|r|$ and make the strength bands non-overlapping: the current wording assigns $0.75$ to both moderate and strong. Qualify the shared-sign claim as applying to the least-squares regression slope with an intercept and defined r; an arbitrary line fitted by eye does not guarantee it. The source contains inconsistent strength labels at lines 2107 and 2316, so those isolated labels should not override the consistent interpretation examples.

removed.reason: Removed the off-booklet range-recognition task because the booklet teaches the range but never asks students to reject an out-of-range coefficient.
Removed the off-booklet gradient-versus-r diagnosis because no comparable booklet question asks students to diagnose this substitution.
Removed the off-booklet explanation of zero correlation for a curve because no comparable booklet question asks this and the solution assumes unstated symmetric sampling.
Removed the off-booklet consistency check between a supplied gradient and r because no comparable booklet question asks this.
Removed the off-booklet explanation of zero correlation for a curve, including its inconsistent count of plotted points.
Removed the off-booklet range-recognition question because recognising an impossible coefficient is not a task asked in the booklet.

summary: Replaced coefficient-ranking tasks and the mastery quiz curve task with cited booklet interpretations, restricted prediction usefulness and mastery interpretation to supported questions, and removed unsupported tasks while retaining all tier minimums. Clarified magnitude as $|r|$, made strength bands non-overlapping, qualified the least-squares shared-sign statement and updated the affected procedure heading without removing theory text.
reviewSummary: All 19 canonical items have correct answers and supported booklet question types, and each quiz has exactly one correct option with valid distractor explanations. The theory is acceptable, all eight removals are justified, and no worked examples were supplied.
